comparisons.reason: Same shared construct (any comment cites specific empirical evidence; same source, binary, 0/1/null rules). Pending differences: index 1 requires the comment to be a 'counter-argument' and adds an explicit exclusion of vague 'studies show' appeals; index 0 has no counter-argument requirement and counts a 'specific documented factual case' while excluding personal anecdote without checkable specifics. Index 1 explicitly includes 'event' and 'documented observation'. These scope and eligibility wording differences need an explicit measurement decision.

Both read only OC_comments and return 1 if any comment itself offers specific empirical evidence (data, statistics, named study/source, documented case) to support its argument. Both exclude pure logic, hypotheticals, opinion, unverifiable anecdote and quoted OP text. Both return 0 when parseable with no qualifying comment and null when missing, empty or unparseable. Wording differences are harmless; index 2 adds 'measured observations', which is minor.
